y5r5xj: The present perfect connects an experience with the present. Form: he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han + participle. With -ar verbs we use -ado; with -er and -ir verbs, -ido. The participle does not change with the person: ellas han viajado. The auxiliary and the participle are not separated by a pronoun: lo he visto.

1fqwcf2: Escribir has the irregular participle escrito; the auxiliary shows the person.
1fyx6an: Ask with alguna vez without requiring a date. Ya shows that something is done; todavía leaves a possibility open; nunca denies an experience. The participles hecho, dicho, visto, escrito, puesto, vuelto, abierto, and roto are irregular. For a finished date, the preterite will appear next week. The use of the perfect varies between regions.
